sources: SUNDAY Sep 27 2026 RUN (06:12 UTC). Markets have been shut since the Friday Sep 25 close, so no new market prints exist and no macro releases landed over the weekend. This run is therefore a VERIFICATION pass over Friday's closes rather than a new read, and two figures were corrected against better sources. CORRECTION 1 - VIX: 14.87, the actual Sep 25 close (-5.11 pct on the day), per Portfolio Terminal's VIX close series. The previous run carried 15.22 from a Schwab intraday market update. Same series shows 15.67 on Sep 24, 15.18 on Sep 23, 14.21 on Sep 22 and 14.87 on Sep 21. Against 14.81 on Sep 18 that makes equity vol FLAT week-over-week, not up about 3 pct as reported yesterday. The trend flag is changed from up to flat. CORRECTION 2 - COPPER/GOLD: 1.56, not 1.57. Copper 6.70 USD/lb (TradingEconomics Sep 25, -0.35 pct), gold 4,285.00 USD/oz (TradingEconomics Sep 25, +0.24 pct); 6.70/4285*1000 = 1.564. The prior run used USAGOLD's 4,280.19 gold print. Rounding difference only, trend stays flat. CONFIRMED AND UPGRADED - CURVE: 2s10s 0.36, now a dated FRED T10Y2Y observation for Sep 25 (updated 4:03 PM CDT Sep 25), matching the 5.17 pct 10y and 4.81 pct 2y in Advisor Perspectives/dshort's Sep 25 Treasury Yields Snapshot. Yesterday this was a calculated figure against a FRED series still dated Sep 24 at 0.31; it is now a primary print. HIGH confidence. Up 9bp from 0.27 a week ago - a fourth straight session of bear steepening. CONFIRMED: Brent 104.32 (TradingEconomics Sep 25, -2.14 pct; yesterday's 104.37 was an intraday read of the same series). Still roughly +20 pct on the month and +51 pct y/y, and up week-over-week, so trend stays up. The Friday drop is on CNBC and Fox Business reports of US-Iran negotiators discussing a phased reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. No weekend follow-through found either way, so the de-escalation remains a headline, not a confirmed deal. CONFIRMED: HY OAS 280bp (FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2, 2.80 pct dated Sep 24, next release Sep 28), up from 270 the prior week. The first genuine widening of this episode and the level flagged in the last three runs as the tell. Trend up, HIGH confidence. CONFIRMED: 5y5y forward inflation 2.34 pct (FRED T5YIFR, Sep 25) versus 2.35 on Sep 21 - flat. Breakevens are still not confirming the oil spike, so the long-end selloff remains a real-rate and term-premium story. CONFIRMED: MOVE 104.58, still the Sep 24 close (Saxo Bank options brief Sep 25, Bloomberg Sep 25 on Treasury vol's biggest jump in a year). Broke 100 for the first time in three months and is up roughly 30 pct in a week. No Sep 25 print retrievable; carried one session. Trend up. CONFIRMED: DXY 101.03 (TradingEconomics Sep 25, -0.25 pct) - first down day after five up, still higher than a week ago, trend up. NFCI -0.555 for the week ending Sep 18 (Chicago Fed via FRED); no new weekly print, next Sep 30, still the loosest of the cycle, flat. CARRIED with no new releases: initial claims 197k for the week ending Sep 19 (DOL, released Sep 24, next Oct 1), ISM manufacturing 54.6 (August, next Oct 1), UMich consumer sentiment 48.1 (final September, released Sep 25, down 7.0 pct from 51.7 in August and a four-month low), building permits 1,403k (August, -2.1 pct m/m, trend down, next Oct 17), LEI y/y about -0.7 pct (August), Sahm rule -0.07 (August, next Oct 2), SOFR-OIS 0bp and EUR/USD 3M cross-currency basis -10bp (standing assumptions, no free live source), global liquidity 1 (stable). BDTI DATA FLAG: carried at 4,899 for a SEVENTH consecutive run. Still no dated Baltic print retrievable - Investing.com remains stale at 1,107 dated 31/03, StockQ shows a Sep 25 row with empty value cells, MacroMicro is gated and the Baltic Exchange is subscription-only. LOW CONFIDENCE; this field should be treated as non-informative until a paid or alternative source is wired in, and it has now been stale long enough to be worth fixing or dropping from the dashboard. PICTURE: nothing moved because nothing could, but the verification pass sharpens rather than softens the read. The curve figure is now a primary FRED print at 0.36 instead of an estimate, so the fourth straight session of bear steepening is solid. HY OAS at 280bp remains the one credit signal that has genuinely repriced. The MOVE-versus-VIX divergence is actually WIDER than yesterday's numbers implied: with VIX corrected to a flat 14.87 rather than a rising 15.22, rates vol is up about 30 pct on the week against equity vol that has not moved at all. That is the cleanest statement of the current setup - the stress is entirely in the rates complex and has begun to leak into credit, while equity vol and NFCI at the loosest of the cycle are the two holdouts. The domestic soft patch is unchanged and unhelpful: UMich 48.1, LEI negative y/y, permits falling, but claims at 197k still showing no labor-market crack, which leaves the policy-error framing intact. WATCH THIS WEEK: HY OAS through 300 (next FRED print Sep 28), whether MOVE holds above 100 once cash trading resumes Monday, whether the Hormuz de-escalation is real or fades, whether the 10y stalls at 5.25, NFCI Sep 30, ISM manufacturing and initial claims Oct 1, Sahm rule Oct 2. SOURCES: FRED/St. Louis Fed (T10Y2Y Sep 25, T5YIFR Sep 25, BAMLH0A0HYM2 Sep 24, NFCI Sep 18), Advisor Perspectives/dshort Treasury Yields Snapshot Sep 25, Saxo Bank Options Brief Sep 25 (MOVE, VIX), Bloomberg Sep 25 (Treasury volatility), Portfolio Terminal VIX close series, TradingEconomics (Brent, copper, gold, DXY), CNBC Sep 24 and Fox Business Sep 25 (Hormuz talks), Chicago Fed, US Department of Labor, Census Bureau/HUD, Conference Board, University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers, ISM, Investing.com and StockQ (BDTI attempts, both unusable).
